title-group.article-title: Planar Ni-N-C Electrodes in Alkaline Flow Cells for High-Rate CO2RR

abstract.p: A planar Ni-N-C catalyst (P-Ni-N-C) pyrolyzed at 800 C was evaluated for CO2RR in a gas-diffusion flow cell using 1.0 M KOH electrolyte.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: An anion-exchange membrane separator (MS) separated the catholyte and anolyte chambers at a flow rate of 10-3 m3/h.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: P-Ni-N-C delivered an initial FE_{\mathrm{CO}} = 94.2\% at -0.6 V vs RHE and 200 mA cm-2, outperforming commercial Ag nanoparticles (83.1% FE) under identical 1.0 M KOH flow-cell conditions, but suffered electrolyte flooding after 12 h (see Figure S2 for raw impedance curves).

caption.p: Flow-cell CO2RR comparison in 1.0 M KOH at -0.6 V vs RHE.
